title: Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract and Diagnostic Playbook
body:
> **Archived 2026-01-12:** this page is superseded by "Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract and Diagnostic Playbook" and is kept for reference only.

Summary:
This page describes the Kernel Snapshot Observability Contract that the serving runtime uses to capture small, deterministic kernel-level state for quick post-hoc diagnostics, profiling correlation, and reproducible benchmarks. It covers what a snapshot contains, TTL/retention, collection cadence, storage indexing, query semantics, and how to use snapshots during incidents and regressions.

Why a formal contract:
- Faster triage: a snapshot gives a compact, self-contained view of kernel scheduling state across shards without needing full traces.
- Reproducible regression hunts: standard fields allow automated delta comparison (hashes/digests) across releases and benchmarks.
- Safe production capture: size and cost limits keep collection cheap and non-disruptive.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: GPU-scheduling kernels, kernel selector hints, active batch queue heads, kvcache hot entry metadata, and per-request token-progress markers. Not a replacement for full GPU traces or perf counters.
- Goals: typically <= 2KB compressed per snapshot per shard, capture latency < 5ms end-to-end, snapshot ingestion availability 99.9%.

Contract: snapshot manifest fields
- manifest_type: "kernel-snapshot-v1" (schema version).
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339 string (time of capture).
- host_id: runtime host identifier (short hash).
- shard_id: logical shard name/id.
- kernel_hint: canonical scheduler kernel name (e.g. "attn_sharded_kv_v2").
- active_requests: comma-separated list of up to 8 request_ids with short metadata (see Active Request Encoding).
- batch_head_shape: concurrency/sequence-length tuple (e.g. "concurrency=12;avg_seq=128").
- kv_hot_prefix_digest: 64-bit hex digest of the most frequent KV prefixes (up to 4, comma-separated).
- queue_depth: integer (queued kernel tasks).
- slot_usage_pct: integer 0-100 (estimated GPU slot occupancy).
- mem_watermark_mb: integer (resident MB attributed to the shard at capture).
- fallback_flags: short tokenized list of active degradation flags (e.g. "quantized-fallback,eviction-throttle").
- capture_id: uuid string (unique per snapshot).
- sample_hash: sha1 hex of the canonicalized manifest (fast equality checks).

Active Request Encoding: up to 8 items, each as request_id|model:ver|priority|est_remaining_tokens
Example: "r1234|redwood/7b:2025-07-01|p2|est32"

Size and performance constraints:
- Uncompressed manifest must be <= 8KB. Producers MUST gzip the payload before upload.
- Capture must never block request latency: sample at scheduling safe points (e.g. pre-dispatch / post-eviction) and keep synchronous work to timestamping and copying small metadata.
- Max capture cadence per shard: 1 snapshot / 10s by default; bursts up to 1/second are allowed during active debugging windows.

Capture lifecycle and TTL semantics:
- Local ephemeral cache: snapshots stay in memory for 30s for immediate correlation with live traces.
- Short-term storage: snapshots are forwarded to an indexed store with 14-day retention for operational triage.
- Long-term archive: snapshots older than 14 days can be kept in cold archive for 90 days when pinned (by capture_id or sample_hash) from a runbook or regression alert.
- Automatic eviction: when store quotas are exceeded, snapshots are evicted oldest-first per host.

Storage & indexing conventions:
- Index keys: sample_hash, capture_id, host_id, shard_id, kernel_hint, timestamp_utc.
- Tags: release_tag (e.g. "canary-2025-10-14"), experiment_id (when an experiment triggered collection), incident_id (when captured during an incident).
- Searchable fields are text-tokenized; sample_hash and kernel_hint must support exact-match filters.

Producer responsibilities and API contract:
1) Capture API (local agent): POST /v1/internal/kernel-snapshot
   - Headers: X-Host-ID, X-Shard-ID, X-Capture-Src (auto|manual|diag).
   - Body: gzip'd manifest (UTF-8).
   - Response: 202 Accepted with JSON {"capture_id":"...","sample_hash":"...","ingest_ts":"..."}.
2) Backoff: after more than 3 consecutive 5xx ingestion errors, the agent switches to local retention only and emits runtime.snapshot.ingest.failures.
3) Priority: manual captures (from a runbook) set X-Capture-Priority: high and are exempt from per-shard cadence limits for a 60s window.

Query and diagnosis workflow (runbook):
1) Triage start: on a latency SLO violation or kernel regression alert, the runbook owner starts a "snapshot-hunt".
2) Pull matching snapshots filtered by sample_hash, kernel_hint, timeframe, release_tag.
3) Delta-compare sample_hash between canary and baseline to locate divergence.
4) If sample_hash matches but the incident continues, escalate to full trace capture by enabling continuous tracing on the affected shards (see profiling-playbook integration).

Integration with profiling playbooks and benchmarking suite:
- Profiling correlation: snapshots act as lightweight join keys for streaming traces and microbenchmarks. Put capture_id in the trace span attribute runtime.kernel_snapshot.capture_id.
- Benchmark gating: nightly benchmarks capture a deterministic snapshot per workload and record sample_hash in the benchmark results CSV. A run where the sample_hash distribution differs from baseline on > 20% of shards raises a quality alert.
- Kernel scheduler experiments: for kernel rollouts, collect baseline/canary snapshot cohorts and run a pairwise hash-difference analysis as part of the release checklist.

Release gating checklist (minimum):
- Collect baseline and canary cohort snapshots for 24 hours, with at least 1000 snapshots per cohort.
- Run the automated sample_hash cluster analysis; no new kernel_hint set may appear in >5% of canary shards unless intended.
- Check that average slot_usage_pct and queue_depth stay within +/- 10% of baseline.
- Sign-off from runtime-scheduling and profiling owners.

Alerting and SLOs:
- Metric: runtime.snapshot.ingest.latency_p50 < 30ms, p95 < 250ms.
- Metric: runtime.snapshot.size_bytes_p95 < 4096 bytes compressed.
- Alert: snapshot-ingest-error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> page infra-oncall.
- Alert: sample_hash-drift-score > 0.2 across canary vs baseline -> notify runtime-release-team.

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Not a full trace: snapshots are deliberately small and omit per-kernel GPU counters. Triage with them, then escalate to detailed tracing.
- Digest collisions: sample_hash is sha1 over a canonicalized manifest; collisions are possible but extremely unlikely. If one is suspected, attach a raw manifest comparison.
- Cost: frequent snapshots on every shard raise storage costs; agents enforce the default cadence and burst limits.

Operational playbook: incident example (step-by-step)
1) Pager fires for high tail latency on model X.
2) Oncall runs "snapshot-query --kernel attn_sharded_kv_v2 --since 5m --format table" across the implicated shards.
3) If sample_hash variance is high between the recent canary and baseline, run the pairwise-diff tool and note the differing fields.
4) If a mem_watermark_mb spike lines up with rising queue_depth, trigger an immediate spillover rollback (see runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook).
5) Capture extended traces for 10 minutes and record the capture_ids of interest.

CLI examples and snippets:
- Query tool (example):
  # list snapshots matching kernel and timeframe
  snapshot-query --kernel "attn_sharded_kv_v2" --since "2025-11-10T12:00:00Z" --limit 200 --output json

- Minimal producer example (bash curl):
  payload=$(printf '{"manifest_type":"kernel-snapshot-v1","timestamp_utc":"%s","host_id":"h-abc123","shard_id":"s1","kernel_hint":"attn_sharded_kv_v2","active_requests":"r1|m:1|p1|est24","batch_head_shape":"concurrency=8;avg_seq=64","kv_hot_prefix_digest":"%s","queue_depth":12,"slot_usage_pct":72,"mem_watermark_mb":12288,"fallback_flags":"none","capture_id":"%s"}' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "deadbeefcafebabe" "$(uuidgen)")
  echo "$payload" | gzip -c | curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "X-Host-ID: h-abc123" -H "X-Shard-ID: s1" --data-binary @- https://internal-ingest.redwood/v1/internal/kernel-snapshot

Appendix A — Example canonical manifest (pretty-printed):
{
  "manifest_type": "kernel-snapshot-v1",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-11-17T09:41:22Z",
  "host_id": "h-0a1b2c",
  "shard_id": "s1",
  "kernel_hint": "attn_sharded_kv_v2",
  "active_requests": "r1234|redwood/7b:2025-07-01|p2|est32,r1240|redwood/7b:2025-07-01|p1|est8",
  "batch_head_shape": "concurrency=12;avg_seq=128",
  "kv_hot_prefix_digest": "0x9f8e7d6c",
  "queue_depth": 4,
  "slot_usage_pct": 68,
  "mem_watermark_mb": 11876,
  "fallback_flags": "quantized-fallback",
  "capture_id": "3c1e9a40-7d2b-4f61-8a0e-5b9c2d7e1f30",
  "sample_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5f6..."
}

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Runtime Observability (oncall: #infra-runtime-observability)
- Reviewers: see metadata above.
- Escalation path: runtime-scheduling -> eng-sre -> infra-ops.

Change history and notes:
